overview.purpose: The Credit Management Policy is designed to standardise lending decisions and to provide a clear guideline on the Society's credit management position and risk appetite.
overview.objectivesIntro: The policy is based on five main objectives.
objectives: Ensure consistency in the processes and procedures used to manage all credit aspects of the Society.
Ensure the adoption of sustainable prudential guidelines in the Society's lending processes.
Ensure that all members are treated fairly when making credit decisions.
Evaluate credit decision-making and adjust it as circumstances arise.
Provide guidelines on the protection of the Society's credit assets and the recovery of delinquent loans to enhance the Society's liquidity and returns on investments.

scope.text: The Society's credit operations shall be only for the benefit of its duly registered members. The Society may, however, grant credit facilities to other Registered Cooperatives as provided by the Nigerian Cooperative Societies Act and the By-law of the CBN Staff Multipurpose Cooperative Society (2026).
All credit transactions of the Society must be within the ambit of all relevant laws and regulations in Nigeria.
This policy provides the minimum requirement for the administration and implementation of the credit objectives of the Society.

funding: Other income generated by the Society
overview.criteriaIntro: Loan requests are granted in line with the following criteria.
criteria: Purpose and utilisation of the loan
Applicant's ability to repay (Maximum Deductible Limit)
Date of employment and date of joining the Cooperative
overview.rejection: Where a loan application fails to meet the prescribed criteria, it is rejected and the applicant is duly notified.

limitPrinciples.text: To manage credit and operational risks, the Society maintains a maximum credit limit (Global and Maximum Deductible limits) on loans to members, based on grade level and ability to pay.
The Credit Committee recommends the global limit for different categories and grade levels of members. The Management Committee reviews the recommended limits and approves them as needed.
The approved global limit is implemented on the Society's application software and communicated to members.
Global limits follow the thresholds set out in Schedule A of the policy.
The Management Committee may review the global limit from time to time.

facilities.name: Special Withdrawal
facilities.summary: A withdrawal from the member's own savings, capped at half of the balance that is not tied to loans.
facilities.description: Savings withdrawal is allowed at a maximum of 50% of the savings balance that is not tied to loans, provided the member has saved continuously for a minimum of six calendar months.
eligibility: The member must have saved continuously for a minimum of six (6) calendar months (2.1.1).
facilities.amountBasis: Maximum of 50% of the savings balance that is not tied to loans.
facilities.tenor: Not applicable. The withdrawal is granted not more than once every 90 days (2.1.2).
facilities.interest: No charge is stated for the withdrawal itself. Where savings are used to liquidate an existing loan, unearned interest applies only if the 50% is sufficient to liquidate all of the member's outstanding loans (2.1.3, 2.1.4).
facilities.security: None stated. The withdrawal is drawn against the member's own savings.
conditions: The Management Committee may allow members to liquidate existing loans, fully or partially, using not more than 50% of their savings balance (2.1.3).
Liquidation of a loan from savings attracts unearned interest only where the 50% of savings balance is sufficient to liquidate all outstanding loans of the member (2.1.4).
facilities.approval: Special withdrawal requests are approved by the General Manager, who may delegate to the Deputy General Manager or Assistant General Manager (3.5.2, 3.5.3).

facilities.name: Normal Loan
facilities.summary: A loan of up to twice the member's savings balance, with a maximum tenor of twelve months.
facilities.description: A Normal Loan may be granted to a member where the loan amount does not exceed two times the member's savings balance, subject to the ability to pay at maturity, regardless of the number of applications, provided the cumulative total remains less than or equal to two times the member's savings balance.
eligibility: Ability to pay at maturity (2.2.1).
Cumulative borrowing, across all applications, within two times the savings balance (2.2.1).
facilities.amountBasis: Not more than two (2) times the member's savings balance, counted cumulatively across applications.
facilities.tenor: Maximum of twelve (12) months. For CBN staff in active service, the tenor is prorated from the date of loan approval to 31 December of the year in which the loan is granted (2.2.3).
facilities.interest: No rate is stated in this clause. Interest rates are recommended by the Investment Committee and approved by the Management Committee (4.4.1).
facilities.security: Where the individual upfront payment is not sufficient to cover the loan, the member tenders collateral. The collateral should be near-cash instruments such as Treasury Bills or COOP Bond Investments, or any other instrument approved by the Management Committee (2.2.2).
facilities.guarantor: Not required. The guarantor requirement in clause 4.6.1 applies to all loans except Normal Loans.
conditions: Approved by any member of the Management Committee (3.1.3).
Repayment period of 12 months runs from the effective date of disbursement (4.1.1).
facilities.approval: Any member of the Management Committee (3.1.3).

facilities.name: Special Loan
facilities.summary: A larger facility for members who have contributed for at least a year, repayable over 36 months.
facilities.description: A Special Loan may be granted to a member who has been contributing for at least one year. The amount granted is not more than three times the member's savings balance, or any amount determined from time to time by the Management Committee.
eligibility: The member has been contributing for at least one (1) year (2.3.1).
Demonstrated ability to repay within a maximum tenor of 36 months (2.3.5).
The facility must not exceed the applicable annual deductible and global limits (2.3.5).
facilities.amountBasis: Not more than three (3) times the member's savings balance, or any amount determined from time to time by the Management Committee (2.3.2).
facilities.tenor: Thirty-six (36) months (2.3.3). The repayment period runs from the effective date of disbursement (4.1.2).
facilities.interest: No rate is stated in this clause. Interest rates are recommended by the Investment Committee and approved by the Management Committee (4.4.1).
facilities.security: Loans above the member's net savings balance must be secured against qualifying pledges provided by the borrowing member (4.8.1).
facilities.guarantor: A member who has not been with the Cooperative for up to five years must provide one (1) suitable guarantor (2.3.4).
conditions: A member may increase a Special Loan subject to clauses 2.3.1, 2.3.2 and 2.3.5 (2.3.6).
Management Committee members recommend Special Loan requests for the President's approval (3.1.4).
facilities.approval: Recommended by the Management Committee for the approval of the President, who may delegate Special Loan approvals to the Vice President, Project, or the Vice President, Policy (3.1.4, 3.1.5).

facilities.name: Quick Credit Loan
facilities.summary: Quick credit of up to 20% of savings, capped by grade, repayable within three months at a flat 2% monthly charge.
facilities.description: Quick Credit is granted provided that the loan amount does not exceed twenty per cent (20%) of the member's savings balance, subject to a maximum of ₦500,000 for Junior Staff, ₦1,000,000 for Senior Staff and ₦2,000,000.00 for Executives. It runs for a maximum of three months and is granted only on satisfactory evidence of the member's ability to repay within the stipulated period.
eligibility: The loan does not exceed 20% of the member's savings balance (2.4.1).
Satisfactory evidence of ability to repay within the stipulated period (2.4.1).
facilities.amountBasis: Up to 20% of the member's savings balance, subject to maximums of ₦500,000 for Junior Staff, ₦1,000,000 for Senior Staff and ₦2,000,000.00 for Executives (2.4.1).
facilities.tenor: Maximum of three (3) months (2.4.1, 2.4.4). Runs from the effective date of disbursement (4.1.4).
facilities.interest: A flat charge of 2% every month (2.4.2).
facilities.security: Members accessing a Quick Loan may be required to pledge for repayment (2.4.3).
facilities.guarantor: Not separately stated. The general guarantor rule applies to all loans except Normal Loans (4.6.1).
conditions: Where a member fails to repay a Quick Credit within three months, it is recovered from the member's savings (2.4.5).
facilities.approval: Approved with other loans by the President; normal loans are excluded (3.2.1).

facilities.name: Investment Loan
facilities.summary: A loan window for income-generating or asset acquisition projects, at four times the member's savings.
facilities.description: This is a loan window the Cooperative avails to willing members who are desirous of borrowing for income-generating or asset acquisition and projects.
eligibility: The loan is subject to the availability of funds, ability to repay and the global limit (2.5.2).
A member who has not been with the Cooperative for five years must provide one guarantor not less than the grade of the applicant (2.5.4).
facilities.amountBasis: Four (4) times the member's savings as at the time of request. The applicable interest rate is determined by the Management Committee, subject to the availability of funds, ability to repay and the global limit (2.5.2).
facilities.tenor: The repayment period shall not exceed four (4) years (2.5.3). Clause 4.1.3 states a maximum repayment period of 60 months for investment loans; the two provisions conflict and are flagged for confirmation (see the verification notes).
facilities.interest: Determined by the Management Committee, subject to the availability of funds, ability to repay and the global limit (2.5.2).
facilities.security: Loans above the member's net savings balance must be secured against qualifying pledges (4.8.1).
facilities.guarantor: One guarantor, not less than the grade of the applicant, where the member has not been with the Cooperative for five years (2.5.4).
conditions: An additional Investment Loan may be granted to a member with an existing Investment Loan, provided the aggregate annual loan repayment obligations, including those arising from the additional loan, do not exceed the maximum deductible limit applicable to the member's grade (2.5.5).
facilities.approval: Approved by the President, with Special and other loans (3.2.1).

facilities.name: Project Loan
facilities.summary: Financing for landed property and buildings with acceptable title, requiring 30% unencumbered savings.
facilities.description: A loan facility made available to eligible members who wish to obtain financing for Cooperative-sponsored projects as well as projects sourced by members from external parties. Project Loans are restricted to landed properties and buildings with acceptable title documents, and are subject to the availability of funds and satisfactory credit appraisal.
eligibility: The property must be landed property or a building with acceptable title documents (2.6.1).
Satisfactory credit appraisal and availability of funds (2.6.1).
A minimum unencumbered savings contribution of thirty per cent (30%) of the project value (2.6.2).
Projects sourced from external parties are subject to satisfactory verification and confirmation of title documents (2.6.4).
facilities.amountBasis: Up to two (2) times the Global Limit applicable to the member's grade, subject to a minimum unencumbered savings contribution of 30% of the project value and to the availability of funds (2.6.2).
facilities.interest: No rate is stated in this clause. Interest rates are recommended by the Investment Committee and approved by the Management Committee (4.4.1).
facilities.security: The land or building financed serves as collateral until the loan is fully repaid, and the original title documents remain in the custody of the Cooperative until the loan is fully discharged (2.6.6). Title documents may include a Certificate of Occupancy (C of O), Right of Occupancy (R of O), Deed of Assignment and Power of Attorney (2.6.4). The borrower executes an irrevocable authority allowing the Society to take possession of, dispose of or sell the financed property on default and to apply the proceeds to the outstanding principal, accrued interest, fees and other charges (2.6.5).
facilities.guarantor: The general guarantor rule applies to all loans except Normal Loans (4.6.1).
conditions: Where a member fails to make the required repayments in full for two (2) consecutive years after disbursement, the Cooperative may revoke the allocation of the land or building and refund the amount paid up to the date of revocation, less an administrative charge of 2 per cent (2%) (2.6.7).
Where a member has an existing loan before applying for a Project Loan, the outstanding balance is deducted from the Project Loan proceeds before the balance is disbursed (2.6.8).
facilities.approval: Approved by the President, with Special and other loans (3.2.1).

facilities.name: End of Service Loan
facilities.summary: A short-term loan for members with less than a year left in the Bank, recovered from gratuity or terminal benefit.
facilities.description: A loan window the Cooperative avails to willing members who have less than one year left in the Bank and who are desirous of borrowing for a short-term purpose. Such loans are recovered from the member's gratuity or terminal benefit.
eligibility: The member has less than one (1) year left in the Bank (2.7.1).

Written confirmation from the CBN Human Resource Department (Pensions Office and Rewards/Benefits Office) that the member's outstanding loan amounts, including the end-of-service loan, will be deducted from the member's final entitlement (2.7.2).
facilities.tenor: Not specified in the policy. The facility is described as being for a short-term purpose (2.7.1).
facilities.interest: Not specified in this clause. Interest rates are recommended by the Investment Committee and approved by the Management Committee (4.4.1).
facilities.security: Recovery is from the member's gratuity or terminal benefit, supported by written confirmation from the CBN Human Resource Department (2.7.1, 2.7.2).
facilities.guarantor: Not separately stated. The general guarantor rule applies to all loans except Normal Loans (4.6.1).
conditions: The member applies in writing to the President, who refers the application to the Credit Committee for consideration (2.7.2).
The Credit Committee reviews the process for applications for this loan from time to time (2.7.3).
facilities.approval: Written application to the President, referred to the Credit Committee for consideration (2.7.2).

facilities.name: Agricultural Loan
facilities.summary: Finance for agricultural production and agro-processing, funded through intervention funds and their terms.
facilities.description: A loan facility made available to eligible members who wish to invest in agricultural production, livestock farming, aquaculture, agro-processing, agricultural value chain activities and other agro-based businesses. The facility is funded through intervention funds sourced by the Cooperative and is subject to the availability of such funds.
eligibility: The member satisfies the terms and conditions governing the intervention fund (2.8.2).
Demonstrated ability to repay, available savings balance, and compliance with the applicable Global and Maximum Deductible Limits (2.8.2).
Payment of the minimum equity contribution prescribed by the intervention fund provider, or as determined by the Cooperative from time to time (2.8.4).
facilities.amountBasis: Determined by the guidelines of the intervention fund provider and the Cooperative's credit assessment of the member's repayment capacity and project viability (2.8.3).
facilities.tenor: In accordance with the terms of the intervention fund and the cash flow cycle of the agricultural enterprise being financed, subject to a maximum tenor approved by the Management Committee (2.8.5).
facilities.interest: Not stated. The facility is governed by the terms and conditions of the intervention fund (2.8.2).
facilities.security: The Cooperative may require appropriate security, including savings balance, agricultural assets, landed property, guarantees, insurance policies, warehouse receipts or any other acceptable collateral. The borrower executes all required loan and security documentation before disbursement (2.8.6).
facilities.guarantor: Guarantees are listed among the acceptable forms of security (2.8.6). The general guarantor rule applies to all loans except Normal Loans (4.6.1).
conditions: Loan proceeds are utilised solely for the approved agricultural purpose. The Cooperative may monitor project implementation, conduct inspections and request periodic reports (2.8.7).
The borrower complies with any insurance, risk-sharing or guarantee requirements prescribed by the intervention fund provider or the Cooperative (2.8.8).

On default, the Cooperative may recover the outstanding balance, accrued interest, fees and other charges through any lawful means, including realisation of pledged collateral, application of the member's savings and guarantees (2.8.9).
facilities.approval: Approved by the President, with Special and other loans (3.2.1).

facilities.name: Loan to Other Registered Cooperatives
facilities.summary: A facility to another registered cooperative society, requiring Management Committee approval and the Registrar's prior approval.
facilities.description: A loan granted to another registered cooperative society is subject to the approval of the Management Committee and the prior approval of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies.
eligibility: The borrower is a registered cooperative society (2.9.1).
Approval of the Management Committee and prior approval of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (2.9.1).
facilities.interest: Not specified in this clause. Interest rates are recommended by the Investment Committee and approved by the Management Committee (4.4.1).
conditions: The Society may also develop other types of credit facilities for the sole benefit of its members, in pursuit of its mission and objectives (2.9.6).
facilities.approval: Management Committee approval, with the prior approval of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (2.9.1).

application.intro: A loan request is assessed against the criteria in clause 1.3.1 before any facility is approved. The requirements below are drawn from the policy and apply according to the facility requested.

items.label: Who may borrow
items.text: The Society's credit operations are only for the benefit of its duly registered members. Credit may also be granted to other registered cooperatives as provided by the Nigerian Cooperative Societies Act and the 2026 By-law.

items.label: Minimum contribution history
items.text: A Special Loan requires at least one year of contributions. A Special Withdrawal requires six calendar months of continuous saving.

items.label: Savings balance sets the ceiling
items.text: Normal Loan: up to two times savings. Special Loan: up to three times savings. Investment Loan: four times savings at the time of request. Quick Credit: up to 20% of savings, within grade caps.

items.label: Project equity
items.text: A Project Loan requires a minimum unencumbered savings contribution of 30% of the project value.

items.label: Savings as a recovery source
items.text: The Society may invoke the right of set-off to repay long outstanding loans from a member's savings balance.

items.label: Maximum Deductible Limit
items.text: The member's ability to repay is assessed against the Maximum Deductible Limit for the grade, and the facility must not exceed the applicable annual deductible and global limits.

items.label: Evidence for short-term credit
items.text: Quick Credit is granted only on satisfactory evidence of the member's ability to repay within the stipulated period.

items.label: Employment and age
items.text: Date of employment, date of joining the Cooperative and date of birth form part of the assessment criteria.

items.label: When a guarantor is required
items.text: A borrowing member who is not up to five years with the Cooperative executes a pledge and furnishes one guarantor who must be a member of the Society, for all loans except Normal Loans.

items.label: Grade of the guarantor
items.text: The guarantor must hold a grade level not lower than one level above that of the borrowing member, and shall not guarantee more than one member at a time.

items.label: Duties of the guarantor
items.text: The guarantor personally guarantees repayment if the borrower defaults, the particulars on which the value of the borrower's securities is based, and that the loan is used for the purpose stated in the application. The guarantor must have a good credit standing with the Society.

items.label: When security is required
items.text: All loan facilities granted to members that are more than their net savings balance must be secured against qualifying pledges provided by the borrowing member.

items.label: Acceptable pledges
items.text: Annual upfront payments, including other allowances within the tenure of the facility; final entitlement or gratuity; liquid or near-cash assets the member owns during and after the tenure, such as Treasury bills, Bond Investment and landed property located in Abuja, Port Harcourt or Lagos with a C of O and other title documents submitted to the Cooperative; and the original property allocation letter issued by the Cooperative, with proper valuation to determine current value.

items.label: Terms disclosed before signing
items.text: The Society states the credit terms and conditions on its loan application e-portal or form, and applicants agree or disagree with those terms in line with the policy.

periods.label: Agricultural Loan
periods.value: Per the intervention fund and the enterprise cash flow, within a maximum approved by the Management Committee

repayment.periodsNote: Each period runs from the effective date of loan disbursement (4.1.1 to 4.1.4). Retirees and pensioners repay any loan granted to them every month (4.1.5).
sources: Monthly deductions from the member's monthly salary
Other sources presented by the member and approved by the Management Committee
repayment.setOff: The Society may invoke the right of set-off to repay long outstanding loans with a member's savings balance (4.2.1).
recall: If a member indicates his or her resignation or retirement.
If a member is dismissed or terminated from the service of CBN.
repayment.penalty: In case of default in repayment, the outstanding loan is rolled over at a new rate determined by the Management Committee, effective from the day after the due date of repayment (4.5.1). The policy does not state a fixed penal percentage; the rate is set by the Management Committee.

recovery.text: Outstanding credit and loan balances are first recovered from the annual allowance bulk payment, then from final entitlements for exiting or deceased members; if a balance remains outstanding, other pledged items provided by the member are used.

The Thrift and Credit unit notifies members of loan maturity dates 30 days before the due date. The written notice advises that a penal interest rate will be applied and that recovery action will commence if the balance remains unpaid after 30 days. The notice is signed by the General Secretary.
The Operations department sends immediate payment request letters to members with balances outstanding after 33 days. The letter is signed by the General Manager.
The Operations department provides the Finance and Accounts department with an ageing report of balances outstanding after 90 days, including the recovery actions taken on each balance.

The Credit Committee advises the Management Committee on the actions to take against members with outstanding balances of 93 days and above, considering the materiality of the balance and a cost-benefit analysis of the action.

Where legal action is recommended, the Compliance Officer sends an advice of legal action notice, signed by the President. These notices are not sent where the outstanding balance is backed by pledges tied to annual allowances sufficient to settle it.

retirees.text: The total amount of loan granted to a retiree, including applicable interest, shall not exceed ninety per cent (90%) of the retiree's combined Savings Balance and Bond Investment Balance.
In determining eligibility, the Society ensures that the total loan obligation, including interest, remains within that limit.
Where a retiree fails to repay as and when due, the outstanding balance, including accrued interest and other charges, is recovered from the retiree's Savings Balance and/or Bond Investment Balance.

pensioners.text: Repayment of all loans granted to pensioners is made through pledged monthly deductions from the pensioner's monthly pension allowance.
At the point of application, the pledged monthly deduction must be sufficient to cover the monthly repayment obligations, including principal and interest, on all existing and proposed loans.
Interest on loans granted to pensioners is calculated on a reducing balance basis.

portfolio.text: The credit policy goal is to minimise the possibility of bad debts and limit credit and loan outstanding days to not more than 30 days.

The Non-Performing Loan rate of the Society shall not exceed 1% at any given time, with appropriate provisions made for non-performing loans in line with relevant accounting standards and the cooperative act.
The unrecovered portion of the maximum deductible limit is deemed long outstanding after 30 days, as specified in the Society's Guideline.

administration.intro: The policy sets out the line of authority, responsibility and reporting for credit management.

items: Has fiduciary responsibility for the Society's credit management (3.1.1).
Approves the Credit Management Policy and any revisions to it (3.1.2).
Approves applications for Normal Loans by qualifying members, through any member of the Committee (3.1.3).
Recommends Special Loan requests for the approval of the President (3.1.4).
Approves interest rate changes and revisions for the Society's loans as recommended by the Investment Committee (3.1.7).
Approves all applications for Special, Investment and other loans except Normal Loans (3.2.1).
May delegate Special Loan approvals to the Vice President, Project, or the Vice President, Policy (3.1.5).
Has authority to approve or reject member loan waiver requests based on the recommendation of the Credit Committee (3.2.2).
Signs advice of legal action notices to members (6.2.10).

roles.composition: The Chairman, who is the Vice President, Policy; the Treasurer; the Financial Secretary; the Compliance Officer; four other members appointed by the Management Committee (one pensioner, one retiree and two serving staff, one of whom is junior staff); and the Assistant Secretary 2 as Secretary. The Head of Operations attends all meetings as a non-voting member (3.3.1).
items: Proposes, reviews and amends existing credit policy for Management Committee approval (3.3.2).
Determines members' debt restructuring terms (3.3.2).
Oversees the thrift and credit operations of the Society (3.3.2).
Makes recommendations on loan waiver requests to the President (3.3.2).
Carries out any other responsibility incidental to the achievement of the Society's credit objectives (3.3.2).
Meets quarterly to review the credit and loans ageing report and provide guidance on recovery of long outstanding balances (6.1.2).
Reports to the Management Committee on the credit profile of the Society at least every quarter or when the need arises (3.4.1).
Is responsible for the strategic management of the thrift and credit operations of the Society (3.4.2).
Oversees the general credit operations at the Secretariat (3.5.1).
Approves all special withdrawal requests made by qualifying members (3.5.2).
May delegate approval for special withdrawal to the Deputy General Manager or Assistant General Manager (3.5.3).
Reports to the General Manager, who in turn reports to the Management Committee (3.6.1).
Is responsible for the execution of the Society's approved credit strategies and policies, including loan application processing, loan collection and recovery for all credit and loan types (3.6.2).
Is responsible for the development of the Society's loan recovery plans (3.6.3).
Reports to the General Manager, who in turn reports to the Management Committee (3.7.1).
Is responsible for the disbursement of the Society's approved loans to members and advises the Treasurer on the liquidity position of the Society (3.7.2).
Is responsible for the implementation of the Society's loan recovery plans (3.7.3).

authorisations: Any two Management Committee members (a combination of A and B signatories) may authorise the disbursement of duly approved loans (3.1.6).
Application for Normal Loans by qualifying members is approved by any member of the Management Committee (3.1.3).

items.text: Insider lending occurs when the Society grants loans or credit facilities to its Management Committee members, its executive management team members and/or its staff members. This excludes loans and advances granted to staff as part of the approved payroll scheme and structure of the Society.
All insider lending must be at the same terms, conditions, credit evaluation criteria and recovery procedures as apply to non-insider members.

Every quarter, the Internal Auditor reports insider-related outstanding balances to the Audit Committee, including the borrower's name, type of credit, approval date, amount outstanding, nature of collateral, due date and performance status.
The Credit Management Policy is reviewed at least every two years, or as the need arises.
All revisions and amendments must be ratified by the Management Committee.

globalLimits.title: Global Limit and Maximum Deductible Limit
globalLimits.intro: Schedule A to the Credit Policy sets the global limit and maximum deductible limit for each grade. The Society maintains these limits on loans to members based on grade level and ability to pay, and implements the approved limits on its application software.
globalLimits.summary: Global limits range from ₦3,200,000.00 for the Others category to ₦45,000,000.00 for Directors. Maximum deductible limits range from ₦1,120,000.00 to ₦15,000,000.00.

faqs.a: Credit operations are only for the benefit of duly registered members of the Society, and other registered cooperatives may be granted facilities as provided by the Nigerian Cooperative Societies Act and the 2026 By-law. Beyond membership, each facility adds its own conditions: a Special Loan needs at least one year of contributions, an Investment Loan needs savings of four times the amount requested, and a Project Loan needs a 30% unencumbered savings contribution.

faqs.q: What types of loan does the Society offer?
faqs.a: The policy sets out Special Withdrawal, Normal Loan, Special Loan, Quick Credit Loan, Investment Loan, Project Loan, End of Service Loan, Agricultural Loan, and loans to other registered cooperative societies. The Society may also develop other credit facilities for the sole benefit of its members.

The amount depends on the facility. A Normal Loan is capped at two times your savings balance, a Special Loan at three times, an Investment Loan at four times, and Quick Credit at 20% of savings within grade caps of ₦500,000 for Junior Staff, ₦1,000,000 for Senior Staff and ₦2,000,000.00 for Executives. A Project Loan is capped at two times the Global Limit for your grade. Every facility is also subject to the Global Limit and Maximum Deductible Limit for your grade in Schedule A.

faqs.q: What happens if my application does not meet the criteria?
faqs.a: The application is rejected and you are duly notified.

faqs.q: How long do I have to repay?
faqs.a: A Normal Loan runs for a maximum of 12 months, a Quick Credit for 3 months, a Special Loan for 36 months, and a Project Loan for up to 8 years. An Agricultural Loan follows the intervention fund's terms and the enterprise's cash flow, within a maximum approved by the Management Committee. For an Investment Loan, clause 2.5.3 says the repayment period shall not exceed four years while clause 4.1.3 states a maximum of 60 months; the Management Committee's current approved position should be confirmed with the Secretariat.

Interest rates on the Society's credit facilities are recommended to the Management Committee by the Investment Committee, reviewed from time to time as economic conditions change, and published annually in line with the By-laws. The policy states a flat charge of 2% every month for Quick Credit, and interest on loans to pensioners is calculated on a reducing balance basis.

Through monthly deductions from salary, members' annual allowances, monthly pension for pensioners, or other sources you present and the Management Committee approves. The Society may also invoke the right of set-off to repay a long outstanding loan from your savings balance.

faqs.q: Can I take another loan while one is still running?
faqs.a: The policy allows specific cases rather than a general right. An additional Investment Loan may be granted to a member with an existing Investment Loan, provided aggregate annual repayment obligations stay within the Maximum Deductible Limit for the grade. A Special Loan may be increased subject to the contribution, amount and repayment provisions. A Normal Loan is granted regardless of the number of applications, provided the cumulative total stays within two times your savings balance. Any additional facility remains subject to the Global and Maximum Deductible Limits.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss a repayment?
faqs.a: The outstanding loan is rolled over at a new rate determined by the Management Committee, effective from the day after the due date. A Quick Credit not repaid within three months is recovered from savings. Balances are recovered first from the annual allowance bulk payment, then from final entitlements, then from other pledged items. The Thrift and Credit unit sends a maturity notice 30 days before the due date, an immediate payment request follows at 33 days, an ageing report at 90 days, and the Credit Committee advises on balances of 93 days and above.

If you have been with the Cooperative for less than five years, you execute a pledge and provide one guarantor who is a member of the Society, for all loans except Normal Loans. The guarantor must hold a grade not lower than one level above yours, must have good credit standing, and may not guarantee more than one member at a time.

faqs.q: What security does the Society accept?
faqs.a: Any facility above your net savings balance must be secured by a qualifying pledge: annual upfront payments including allowances within the loan tenure, your final entitlement or gratuity, liquid or near-cash assets such as Treasury bills, Bond Investment and landed property in Abuja, Port Harcourt or Lagos with a C of O and title documents, or the original property allocation letter issued by the Cooperative, properly valued.

faqs.q: What security applies to a Project Loan?
faqs.a: The land or building financed is the collateral until the loan is fully repaid, and the original title documents stay with the Cooperative until discharge. The borrower also executes an irrevocable authority allowing the Society to take possession of, dispose of or sell the property on default and apply the proceeds to the outstanding principal, interest, fees and charges.

faqs.q: Can I withdraw part of my savings?
faqs.a: Yes, up to 50% of the savings balance that is not tied to loans, provided you have saved continuously for at least six calendar months, and not more than once every 90 days. The Management Committee may also allow you to liquidate an existing loan, fully or partially, using not more than 50% of your savings balance.

faqs.q: What happens when I retire or leave the Bank?
faqs.a: All outstanding loan balances are liquidated if you indicate resignation or retirement, or if you are dismissed or terminated from CBN service. For a retiree, the total loan including interest may not exceed 90% of the combined Savings Balance and Bond Investment Balance, and any unpaid balance is recovered from those balances.

faqs.q: Can I borrow in my last year of service?
faqs.a: Yes, through the End of Service Loan, which is available to members with less than one year left in the Bank who need short-term funding. You apply in writing to the President, who refers it to the Credit Committee, and you are cleared once CBN Human Resource Department confirms in writing that your outstanding loans, including this one, will be deducted from your final entitlement. The loan is recovered from your gratuity or terminal benefit.

Through pledged monthly deductions from the monthly pension allowance. At application, the pledged deduction must be enough to cover principal and interest on all existing and proposed loans. Interest on loans to pensioners is calculated on a reducing balance basis.

Normal Loans are approved by any member of the Management Committee. Special, Investment and other loans are approved by the President, who may delegate Special Loan approvals to the Vice President, Project or the Vice President, Policy. Disbursement of an approved loan is authorised by any two Management Committee members (a combination of A and B signatories).

faqs.q: How is the policy kept current?
faqs.a: The Credit Management Policy is reviewed at least every two years, or as the need arises, and all revisions must be ratified by the Management Committee. The Management Committee may also review the global limits from time to time.

flags.issue: Clause 2.5.3 states the repayment period shall not exceed four (4) years, while clause 4.1.3 states a maximum repayment period of 60 (sixty) months for investment loans. The website shows both and flags the conflict rather than choosing one.
Section 5.0.0 is headed Loan Account Review and Recovery, but its subsections are numbered 6.1.0 Loans Review and 6.2.0 Recovery, and the table of contents lists them the same way.
Clause 2.9.0 runs from 2.9.1 directly to 2.9.6. Clauses 2.9.2 to 2.9.5 are absent from the document.
Clause 2.8.10, inside the Agricultural Loan section, repeats the Project Loan clause on deducting an existing loan balance from Project Loan proceeds.
Clause 3.3.1 reads 'Four (1) other members', then lists one pensioner, one retiree and two serving staff. The count is ambiguous and is reproduced in the website as written.
The document control block is numbered 2.5.5 but appears after section 10.0.0 with the approvals, which does not follow the section sequence.
Clause 4.5.1 rolls a defaulted loan to a new rate determined by the Management Committee, and clause 6.2.4 refers to a penal interest rate, but no fixed percentage is stated in the document.

The document is issue-dated August 2026 and the President signed approval on 10 August 2026, but no commencement or effective date clause appears. The website states the issue month and asks the Secretariat for the commencement position rather than assuming a date.

The Executive cap in clause 2.4.1 is printed as '2,000,000.00' without the naira symbol used for the other two caps. It is presented as naira on the website, consistent with the clause, and the printed value is unchanged.
Schedule A includes a final row for 'OTHERS' whose membership is not defined anywhere in the policy.

Clauses 2.3.4, 2.5.4 and 4.6.1 express the guarantor threshold as a member 'not up to five years' or 'who has not been with the Cooperative for five years', which reads as under five years of membership. The website states it that way and flags it for confirmation.
